subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

choices: She go to school every day.
She goes to school every day.
She going to school every day.
She is go to school every day.

solution.correct_choice: She goes to school every day.

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Present Simple - for habits and routines.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body: With he/she/it → add -s or -es to the verb!

explanation.title: How it works
explanation.body:
I go → She goes
   ↑        ↑
  (no s)   (+s)

explanation.title: Signal words
explanation.body: 'every day' = routine = Present Simple

explanation.title: Remember
explanation.body:
I/you/we/they → go
he/she/it → goes

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• 'She go' (missing -s)
• 'She is go' (wrong structure)
• 'She going' (missing 'is' for continuous)

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: She goes to school every day.

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

choices: Look! The cat sleep on the sofa.
Look! The cat sleeps on the sofa.
Look! The cat is sleeping on the sofa.
Look! The cat slept on the sofa.

solution.correct_choice: Look! The cat is sleeping on the sofa.

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Present Continuous - for actions happening RIGHT NOW.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body:
'Look!' = something is happening NOW
→ Use Present Continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing

explanation.title: Structure
explanation.body:
[am/is/are] + [verb + ing]
The cat is sleeping
      ↑     ↑
     is   -ing

explanation.title: Signal words
explanation.body:
Look! Listen! Right now! At the moment!
→ Present Continuous!

explanation.title: Comparison
explanation.body:
• Every day → Present Simple (habit)
• Right now → Present Continuous (now)

explanation.title: Common mistake
explanation.body: Using Present Simple for current actions!

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: Look! The cat is sleeping on the sofa.

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct sentence for yesterday.

choices: I am walking to school yesterday.

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Past Simple - for completed actions in the past.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body: 'yesterday' = past = Past Simple

explanation.title: How to form
explanation.body:
Regular verbs: add -ed
walk → walked
play → played

explanation.title: Signal words
explanation.body:
yesterday, last week, ago, in 2020
→ Past Simple!

explanation.title: Remember
explanation.body:
Past Simple is the SAME for all persons:
I walked, you walked, he walked, we walked

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• 'I walk yesterday' (wrong tense)
• 'I was walked' (wrong structure)

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: I walked to school yesterday.

subject: EN
prompt: Yesterday I ___ my homework and ___ TV.

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Past Simple with irregular verb (do → did).

explanation.title: Irregular verbs
explanation.body:
Some verbs don't add -ed!
do → did (NOT 'doed'!)
see → saw
go → went

explanation.title: REGULAR vs IRREGULAR
explanation.body:
• watch → watched (regular: +ed)
• do → did (irregular: changes completely)

explanation.title: Common irregular verbs
explanation.body:
do → did
go → went
see → saw
have → had
make → made
get → got

explanation.title: Important
explanation.body: You MUST memorize irregular verbs!

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: did / watched

subject: EN
prompt: Which signal word indicates Present Simple?

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Signal words help you choose the right tense!

explanation.title: PRESENT SIMPLE (habits)
explanation.body:
• every day/week/Monday
• always, usually, often
• sometimes, never

explanation.title: PRESENT CONTINUOUS (now)
explanation.body:
• right now
• at the moment
• Look! Listen!

explanation.title: PAST SIMPLE (finished)
explanation.body:
• yesterday
• last week/year
• ago
• in 2020

explanation.title: Trick
explanation.body: 'every...' = routine = Present Simple

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: every Monday

subject: EN
prompt: Complete: 'She ___ (not/like) pizza.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Present Simple negative with he/she/it.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body:
he/she/it → doesn't + base verb
(NOT 'don't'!)

explanation.title: Structure
explanation.body:
[doesn't] + [verb (no s!)]
She doesn't like
     ↑         ↑
  doesn't   no 's'!

explanation.title: Full pattern
explanation.body:
I/you/we/they don't like
he/she/it doesn't like

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• 'She don't like' (wrong helper)
• 'She doesn't likes' (double s!)

explanation.title: Remember
explanation.body: The 's' goes to 'doesn't', NOT to the verb!

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: doesn't like

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct question.

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Yes/No questions in Present Simple.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body: [Do/Does] + [subject] + [base verb]?

explanation.title: Structure
explanation.body:
Do you like pizza?
↓   ↓    ↓
Do  you  like (base form!)

explanation.title: When to use which
explanation.body:
• I/you/we/they → DO you like?
• he/she/it → DOES she like?

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• 'Like you pizza?' (missing Do)
• 'Does you like?' (wrong match: Does + you)
• 'Do you likes?' (verb shouldn't have -s)

explanation.title: Word order
explanation.body:
Statement: You like pizza.
Question: Do you like pizza?

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: Do you like pizza?

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct question.

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Questions with he/she/it in Present Simple.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body: he/she/it → DOES + base verb (no -s!)

explanation.title: Structure
explanation.body:
Does she like coffee?
  ↓    ↓    ↓
Does  she  like (NOT likes!)

explanation.title: Remember
explanation.body:
The 's' is already in 'Does'!
Does + like (NOT likes)

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• 'Does she likes?' (double -s!)
• 'Do she like?' (wrong: Do + she)

explanation.title: Comparison
explanation.body:
Statement: She likes coffee.
Question: Does she like coffee?
          ↑ The 's' moved to 'Does'!

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: Does she like coffee?

subject: EN
prompt: Make a question: 'You went to Berlin.' → '___?'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Past Simple questions.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body: [Did] + [subject] + [base verb]?

explanation.title: Structure
explanation.body:
Did you go to Berlin?
 ↓   ↓   ↓
Did  you  go (BASE form, not 'went'!)

explanation.title: Important
explanation.body:
'Did' already shows past tense!
The main verb goes back to BASE form:
went → go

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• 'Did you went?' (double past!)
• 'Do you went?' (wrong tense)

explanation.title: Comparison
explanation.body:
Statement: You went to Berlin.
Question: Did you go to Berlin?
               ↑ Back to base form!

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: Did you go to Berlin?

subject: EN
prompt: Complete the short answer: 'Do you speak English?' - 'Yes, ___.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Short answers in English.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body: Answer with the SAME helper verb!

explanation.title: Pattern
explanation.body:
Do you...? → Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Does she...? → Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.
Did they...? → Yes, they did. / No, they didn't.

explanation.title: Why short answers
explanation.body:
In English, just 'Yes/No' sounds incomplete!
'Yes' is okay, but 'Yes, I do' is better.

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• 'Yes, I speak' (not wrong, but not natural)
• 'Yes, I am' (wrong helper verb)

explanation.title: Remember
explanation.body: The helper verb in the question = helper verb in answer!

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: I do

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the best option: 'You ___ wear a helmet when you ride a bike.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Modal verbs - 'must' for rules and obligations.

explanation.title: Modal meanings
explanation.body:
• can = ability (Ich kann...)
• must = obligation/rule (Ich muss...)
• should = advice (Ich sollte...)
• might = possibility (vielleicht)

explanation.title: Context
explanation.body:
Helmet when riding = safety RULE
→ must (you HAVE to!)

explanation.title: Structure
explanation.body:
Modal verbs + BASE VERB (no 'to'!)
You must wear (NOT 'to wear')

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• 'You must to wear' (no 'to' needed!)
• Using 'can' for rules (can = ability, not rule)

explanation.title: Remember
explanation.body: Modals never change: he must, she must, they must (NOT 'musts'!)

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: must

subject: EN
prompt: '___ you help me with my homework?'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Modal verbs - 'can' for requests and ability.

explanation.title: 'can' uses
explanation.body:
1. Ability: I can swim. (Ich kann schwimmen.)
2. Permission: Can I go? (Darf ich gehen?)
3. Request: Can you help? (Kannst du helfen?)

explanation.title: Here
explanation.body:
Asking for help = polite request
→ Can you help me?

explanation.title: Comparison
explanation.body:
• Can you...? = friendly request
• Must you...? = not natural for requests
• Could you...? = more formal/polite

explanation.title: Don't confuse
explanation.body: 'Can' (Können) ≠ 'Must' (Müssen)

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: Can

subject: EN
prompt: 'You ___ eat more vegetables. It's good for your health.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Modal verbs - 'should' for advice.

explanation.title: 'SHOULD' = Advice (Ratschlag)
explanation.body: It's a GOOD IDEA, but not a strict rule.

explanation.title: Context
explanation.body:
'good for your health' = advice, recommendation
→ should (you SHOULD do this)

explanation.title: Comparison
explanation.body:
• must = you HAVE to (Pflicht)
• should = it's a good idea (Empfehlung)
• can = you are able to (Fähigkeit)

explanation.title: German translation
explanation.body:
should ≈ sollte
must ≈ muss

explanation.title: Note
explanation.body: 'Should' is softer than 'must'!

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: should

subject: EN
prompt: Match the words with the meaning.

pairs: a place to wait for a train

bags and suitcases you take on a trip

subject: EN
prompt: What does 'departure' mean?

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Travel vocabulary - departure vs arrival.

explanation.title: DEPARTURE (Abfahrt/Abflug)
explanation.body:
= when you LEAVE
• departure time = Abfahrtszeit
• departure gate = Abflug-Gate

explanation.title: ARRIVAL (Ankunft)
explanation.body:
= when you ARRIVE
• arrival time = Ankunftszeit

explanation.body:
• DEpart = leave (DE- like 'weg-')
• ARrive = come (like 'ankommen')

explanation.title: At airports
explanation.body:
Departures = where you check in to LEAVE
Arrivals = where people COME from flights

explanation.body: when you leave

prompt: What is a 'timetable'?

Monday 8:00 - Math

subject: EN
prompt: Which word means 'Frühstück'?

explanation.body: Daily life vocabulary - meals.

explanation.title: BREAKFAST (Frühstück)
explanation.body:
= the FIRST meal of the day (morning)
break + fast = 'breaking the fast' from sleeping

subject: EN
prompt: Read: 'Tom missed the bus, so he arrived late. The teacher was not angry because Tom had a note from his mother.' What is true?

choices: Tom arrived late and had an excuse.

solution.correct_choice: Tom arrived late and had an excuse.

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Reading comprehension - finding facts in a text.

explanation.title: Text analysis
explanation.body:
'Tom missed the bus' → He was late
'arrived late' → confirms he was late
'not angry because Tom had a note' → he had an excuse

explanation.title: Check each answer
explanation.body:
• 'arrived early' → FALSE (text says 'late')
• 'arrived late and had an excuse' → TRUE ✓
• 'teacher was angry' → FALSE (text says 'not angry')
• 'missed the train' → FALSE (text says 'bus')

explanation.title: Reading tip
explanation.body:
Look for EXACT words in the text!
'bus' ≠ 'train'
'not angry' ≠ 'angry'

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: Tom arrived late and had an excuse.

subject: EN
prompt: Read: 'Dear Lisa, I can't come to your party on Saturday. I have to visit my grandmother. Sorry! Love, Anna.' Why can't Anna come?

choices: She has to visit her grandmother.

solution.correct_choice: She has to visit her grandmother.

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Reading comprehension - understanding a message.

explanation.title: Text analysis
explanation.body:
'I can't come to your party'
'I have to visit my grandmother'
→ The reason is clearly stated!

explanation.title: Reading strategy
explanation.body:
Find the REASON:
'I can't come' = what she can't do
'I have to...' = why (the reason)

explanation.title: Text type
explanation.body:
This is a short MESSAGE (informal note).
• 'Dear Lisa' = greeting
• 'Love, Anna' = closing

explanation.title: TIP
explanation.body: In short texts, the answer is usually directly stated!

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: She has to visit her grandmother.

subject: EN
prompt: Read: 'Subject: Meeting tomorrow. Hi team, the meeting is at 10 a.m. in Room 5. Please bring your notes. Best, Mr. Smith.' When is the meeting?

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Reading emails - finding specific information.

explanation.title: Email structure
explanation.body:
• Subject line: 'Meeting tomorrow'
• Greeting: 'Hi team'
• Body: time, place, request
• Closing: 'Best, Mr. Smith'

explanation.title: Finding information
explanation.body:
Time: 'at 10 a.m.'
Place: 'in Room 5'
Request: 'Please bring your notes'

explanation.title: Email reading tip
explanation.body:
Scan for KEY WORDS:

• Time words (a.m., p.m.)

subject: EN
prompt: Fix the sentence: 'He dont like football.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Error correction - Present Simple negative.

explanation.title: The error
explanation.body:
'He dont like' → TWO mistakes!
1. 'dont' should be 'doesn't' (he/she/it)
2. Missing apostrophe

explanation.title: Correct form
explanation.body:
he/she/it + doesn't + base verb
He doesn't like
     ↑         ↑
  doesn't   no -s!

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• 'doesn't likes' → double marking!
• 'don't' with he/she/it → wrong helper
• 'not like' → missing helper verb

explanation.title: Rule
explanation.body: The -s goes to 'doesn't', NOT the main verb!

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: He doesn't like football.

subject: EN
prompt: Fix the sentence: 'Yesterday I go to the cinema.'

choices: Yesterday I goes to the cinema.
Yesterday I went to the cinema.
Yesterday I am go to the cinema.
Yesterday I going to the cinema.

solution.correct_choice: Yesterday I went to the cinema.

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Error correction - Past Simple.

explanation.title: The error
explanation.body:
'Yesterday' = past time
'go' = present form
→ Tense mismatch!

explanation.title: Correction
explanation.body: go → went (irregular verb!)

explanation.title: Irregular verb
explanation.body:
go - went - gone
NOT: go - goed - goed!

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• Using present tense with past time words
• 'goed' (go is irregular!)

explanation.title: Signal word check
explanation.body: Yesterday = PAST → use PAST tense!

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: Yesterday I went to the cinema.

subject: EN
prompt: Fix the sentence: 'She can to swim very well.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Error correction - Modal verbs.

explanation.title: The error
explanation.body:
'can to swim' → 'to' is wrong!
Modal verbs DON'T use 'to'!

explanation.title: Correct structure
explanation.body:
[modal] + [base verb] (NO 'to'!)
She can swim
    ↑    ↑
  can  swim (not 'to swim')

explanation.title: Modal verbs
explanation.body:
can, must, should, will, would, might
→ ALL followed by BASE VERB, no 'to'!

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• 'can to swim' → remove 'to'
• 'cans swim' → modals don't add -s!
• 'can swims' → base verb, no -s!

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: She can swim very well.

subject: EN
prompt: Complete: 'My name ___ Lisa.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: The verb 'to be' - basic introduction.

explanation.title: 'be' forms
explanation.body:
• I am
• you are
• he/she/it is
• we are
• they are

explanation.title: Here
explanation.body:
'My name' = it (a thing)
→ My name IS Lisa

explanation.title: Common phrases
explanation.body:
• My name is...
• I am... years old
• I am from...

explanation.title: Shortcut
explanation.body: If it's not I/you/we/they, use 'is'!

explanation.title: Don't say
explanation.body:
'My name am Lisa' ✗
'My name are Lisa' ✗

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: is

subject: EN
prompt: Complete: 'A car is ___ than a bike.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Comparatives - comparing two things.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body:
Short adjectives (1-2 syllables) → add -er
fast → faster
tall → taller

explanation.title: Structure
explanation.body:
[adjective + er] + than
A car is faster than a bike.

explanation.title: Spelling rules
explanation.body:
• fast → faster
• big → bigger (double consonant)
• happy → happier (y → i)

explanation.title: Long adjectives
explanation.body:
3+ syllables → more + adjective
• beautiful → more beautiful
• NOT 'beautifuler'!

explanation.title: Remember
explanation.body:
Comparing TWO things = -er or 'more'
Superlative (THE best) = -est or 'most'

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: faster

subject: EN
prompt: Complete: 'This is the ___ book I have ever read.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Superlative + irregular adjective.

explanation.title: 'the ___' = superlative
explanation.body: Comparing more than 2 → superlative (the -est)

explanation.title: Irregular forms
explanation.body:
good → better → best
bad → worse → worst
many → more → most

explanation.title: Structure
explanation.body:
the + superlative
'the best book'

explanation.title: Common mistakes
explanation.body:
• 'the most good' ✗ (good is irregular!)
• 'the better' ✗ (that's comparative)
• 'more good' ✗ (irregular!)

explanation.title: Memorize
explanation.body:
good - better - best
bad - worse - worst

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: best

subject: EN
prompt: Which tense is used for habits and regular actions? Example: 'I usually watch TV in the evening.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Identifying the Simple Present tense.

explanation.title: Simple present - uses
explanation.body:
• Habits and routines (Gewohnheiten)
• General facts (Fakten)
• Regular actions (regelmäßige Handlungen)

explanation.title: Formation
explanation.body:
Infinitive (+ -s/-es for he/she/it)
I watch → He watches

explanation.title: Signal words
explanation.body:
• usually, sometimes, always
• every day, often, never
• on Mondays, in the morning

explanation.title: Examples
explanation.body:
• I usually watch TV. (Gewohnheit)
• The sun rises in the east. (Fakt)
• She works in Berlin. (regelmäßig)

explanation.title: NOT
explanation.body:
• Present Progressive = NOW (gerade jetzt)
• Present Perfect = connection past-present

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: Simple Present

subject: EN
prompt: Which tense is correct? 'I have just arrived at the airport.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Identifying the Present Perfect tense.

explanation.title: Present perfect - uses
explanation.body:
• Action just completed (gerade abgeschlossen)
• Past action with present result
• Experience (Erfahrung)

explanation.title: Formation
explanation.body: have/has + past participle (3rd form)

explanation.title: Analysis
explanation.body:
'I HAVE just ARRIVED'
  ↓           ↓
have    +  past participle
= PRESENT PERFECT

explanation.title: Signal words
explanation.body:
• just, recently (gerade)
• yet, already, still
• since, for
• ever, never

explanation.title: Examples
explanation.body:
• I have just finished. (gerade fertig)
• She has lived here since 2010. (seit)
• Have you ever been to London? (jemals)

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: Present Perfect

subject: EN
prompt: Which tense is correct? 'They are calling their grandma right now.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Identifying the Present Progressive tense.

explanation.title: Present progressive - uses
explanation.body:
• Action happening NOW (jetzt gerade)
• Temporary situation
• Fixed plans (feste Pläne)

explanation.title: Formation
explanation.body: to be (am/is/are) + verb + -ing

explanation.title: Analysis
explanation.body:
'They ARE CALLING their grandma right now.'
      ↓    ↓
   are + calling (-ing)
= PRESENT PROGRESSIVE

explanation.title: Signal words
explanation.body:
• right now, now
• at the moment
• currently
• Look! Listen!

explanation.title: Examples
explanation.body:
• I am studying right now. (gerade jetzt)
• She is working at the moment. (im Moment)
• Look! It is raining! (Schau!)

explanation.title: NOT Simple Present
explanation.body:
'They call' = habit/regularly
'They are calling' = right now

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: Present Progressive

subject: EN
prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct form: 'She ___ (go) to school every day.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Simple Present with he/she/it.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body: Simple Present + he/she/it → add -s or -es

explanation.title: Why 'goes'
explanation.body:
1. 'every day' = Signal for Simple Present ✓
2. 'She' = 3rd person singular
3. go → goes (add -es)

explanation.title: Spelling rules for -s/-es
explanation.body:
• Most verbs: add -s (play → plays)
• Verbs ending in -s, -sh, -ch, -x, -o: add -es
  go → goes
  watch → watches
  wash → washes
• Verbs ending in consonant + y: y → ies
  study → studies
  try → tries

explanation.title: NOT
explanation.body:
• 'is going' = Present Progressive (NOW)
• 'has gone' = Present Perfect

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: goes

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Simple Past form of 'go'?

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Irregular verb: go - went - gone

explanation.title: Irregular verbs
explanation.body:
They don't follow the regular -ed pattern!
You must memorize them.

explanation.title: GO (irregular verb)
explanation.body:
Simple Present: go/goes
Simple Past: went
Past Participle: gone

explanation.title: Usage
explanation.body:
• 'I went to school yesterday.' (Simple Past)
• 'I have gone home.' (Present Perfect)

explanation.title: Common mistake
explanation.body:
'goed' is WRONG! ❌
'go' is irregular → 'went'

explanation.title: More irregular verbs
explanation.body:
• see → saw → seen
• come → came → come
• take → took → taken
• write → wrote → written

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: went

prompt: What is the Past Participle of 'write'?

Irregular verbs don't use -ed!

prompt: Match the verbs with their Simple Past forms.

explanation.title: The matches
explanation.body:

explanation.title: Full forms

explanation.body:

subject: EN
prompt: Which sentence uses the Present Perfect correctly?

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Correct use of Present Perfect with 'since'.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body:
SINCE + point in time → PRESENT PERFECT
FOR + duration → PRESENT PERFECT

explanation.title: 'I have lived here since 2020.'
explanation.body: Present Perfect + since = CORRECT!

explanation.title: 'I have lived here yesterday.'
explanation.body: yesterday = finished time → Simple Past needed!

explanation.title: 'I lived here since 2020.'
explanation.body: since = needs Present Perfect!

explanation.title: 'I am living here since 2020.'
explanation.body: since = needs Present Perfect, not Progressive!

explanation.title: SINCE vs. FOR
explanation.body:
• SINCE + point: since 2020, since Monday, since 3pm
• FOR + duration: for 5 years, for 2 hours, for a week

explanation.title: Examples
explanation.body:
• I have worked here since January.
• I have worked here for 6 months.

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: I have lived here since 2020.

subject: EN
prompt: Which is the correct question form? 'She likes pizza.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Forming questions in Simple Present.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body: Do/Does + subject + infinitive (without -s)?

explanation.title: Formation
explanation.body:
Statement: She likes pizza.
Question: Does she like pizza?

explanation.title: DO vs. DOES
explanation.body:
• DO for I, you, we, they
• DOES for he, she, it

explanation.title: Important
explanation.body:
When using DOES, the main verb loses the -s!
• She likes → Does she like? ✓
• NOT: Does she likes? ❌

explanation.title: More examples
explanation.body:
• He plays tennis. → Does he play tennis?
• They work here. → Do they work here?
• You speak German. → Do you speak German?

explanation.title: Wrong forms
explanation.body:
• 'Do she like?' - wrong helper
• 'Is she like?' - 'be' only for be-verbs/progressive
• 'Like she?' - missing do/does

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: Does she like pizza?

subject: EN
prompt: Which is the correct negative form? 'I like spinach.'

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Forming negations in Simple Present.

explanation.title: The rule
explanation.body: Subject + do/does + not + infinitive

explanation.title: Formation
explanation.body:
Positive: I like spinach.
Negative: I do not like spinach.
Short form: I don't like spinach.

explanation.title: DON'T vs. DOESN'T
explanation.body:
• DON'T (do not) for I, you, we, they
• DOESN'T (does not) for he, she, it

explanation.title: Examples
explanation.body:
• I don't like spinach. (I)
• She doesn't like spinach. (she)
• They don't work here. (they)
• He doesn't play tennis. (he)

explanation.title: Wrong forms
explanation.body:
• 'I doesn't like' - wrong helper for 'I'
• 'I not like' - missing do/does
• 'I no like' - 'no' is not for verbs

explanation.title: Short forms
explanation.body:
• do not = don't
• does not = doesn't

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: I don't like spinach.

subject: EN
prompt: Which modal verb expresses ABILITY (Fähigkeit)?

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Modal verbs and their meanings.

explanation.title: Examples
explanation.body:
• I can swim. (Ich kann schwimmen.)
• She can speak German. (Sie kann Deutsch sprechen.)
• Can you help me? (Kannst du mir helfen?)

explanation.title: Overview of modals
explanation.body:
• CAN = ability, possibility (können)
• MUST = obligation, necessity (müssen)
• SHOULD = advice, recommendation (sollte)
• MAY = permission, possibility (dürfen, könnte)

explanation.title: More examples
explanation.body:
• You must wear a seatbelt. (Pflicht)
• You should study more. (Rat)
• May I go to the toilet? (Erlaubnis)

explanation.title: Grammar rule
explanation.body:
Modal + infinitive WITHOUT 'to'!
• I can swim. ✓
• I can to swim. ❌

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: can

subject: EN
prompt: What is the comparative form of 'big'?

explanation.title: What is this
explanation.body: Comparative adjectives - comparing two things.

explanation.title: The rule for short adjectives
explanation.body: Adjective + -er

explanation.title: Formation
explanation.body: big → bigger

explanation.title: Spelling rule
explanation.body:
Short adjective ending in consonant-vowel-consonant:
Double the last consonant!
big → bigger (not biger!)
hot → hotter
thin → thinner

explanation.title: More short adjectives
explanation.body:
• small → smaller
• tall → taller
• fast → faster
• old → older

explanation.title: LONG ADJECTIVES (3+ syllables)
explanation.body:
Use 'more' + adjective
• beautiful → more beautiful
• interesting → more interesting

explanation.title: Wrong forms
explanation.body:
• 'more big' - big is short, use -er
• 'biger' - need to double the g
• 'biggest' - that's superlative (best of all)

explanation.title: Answer
explanation.body: bigger

subject: EN

explanation.body: Error correction - do/does in negations.

explanation.body:

explanation.title: The error
explanation.body:
'She don't like coffee.' ❌
'She' = 3rd person singular → needs DOESN'T

explanation.title: Correct sentence
explanation.body: 'She doesn't like coffee.' ✓

explanation.title: Why not 'likes'
explanation.body:
After doesn't, use the infinitive (base form)!

explanation.body:
